description: Campaign-bound sigma detection for the "Miasma" / "Phantom Gyp" npm supply-chain worm (StepSecurity + Snyk disclosure, 2026-06-03; a descendant of the Shai-Hulud worm family, distinct from the earlier Mini Shai-Hulud / Nx campaign cluster already in this corpus). Compromised 57 npm packages across 286+ malicious versions in a rolling campaign under two hours, first observed via `@vapi-ai/server-sdk` (408,000+ monthly downloads). Attack mechanism ("Phantom Gyp"): a 157-byte `binding.gyp` file abuses node-gyp's `<!(...)` command-substitution syntax to run an arbitrary shell command during the gyp CONFIGURE phase, before any compiler runs -- `"sources": ["<!(node index.js > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo stub.c)"]` with `"type": "none"` (nothing is actually compiled; the command's side effect is the point). npm auto-invokes `node-gyp rebuild` whenever it sees a `binding.gyp` file, and this happens WITHOUT declaring any preinstall/postinstall lifecycle script in `package.json` -- invisible to tooling that only watches install-hook fields. The `index.js` payload that runs is a 4.5MB obfuscated loader (ROT-14, then AES-128-GCM self-decryption) that downloads and executes a Bun runtime binary (`bun-v1.3.13`) to run the actual 649KB credential-stealer payload under Bun instead of Node -- process-tree monitoring that only watches for `node.exe` child processes never sees the credential-theft stage. Fourth vector of the Nx campaign supply-chain cluster (related vectors in this corpus: Mini Shai-Hulud npm + s1ngularity Nx CLI + nx-console VS Code extension).
